newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Cyprus protests against visits by Turkish warships.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus protests against visits by Turkish warships.

text.p: Cyprus has protested to Secretary-General Kofi Annan over a recent visit to the island by nine Turkish warships "in violation of the territorial integrity and sovereignty of the Republic of Cyprus."

In a letter circulated on Monday, Cypriot U.N. envoy Nicos Agathocleous said two Turkish naval vesels, two submarines and one destroyer docked at the port of Famagusta and three missile boats and one submarine docked in Kyrenia's harbour.

He said that "following the Turkish invasion in 1974 and the occupation of a large part of territory of the Republic of Cyprus, the ports of Famagusta, Karavostasi and Kyrenia were declared closed by the government to all vessels."

He said "these new Turkish actions are especially provocative" since they took place at a time when Annan was making efforts to hold direct talks between President Glafcos Clerides and Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash. The talks are to be held in the New York area from July 9 to 13.
